objective: Define the Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) for absolute beginners who have plateaued, detail primary pain points, and craft the positioning statement and UVP.

demographics.occupations: Software engineers, product managers, finance professionals, healthcare workers, college students
demographics.timeCommitment: 15 to 25 minutes per day, typically during commute, lunch, or evening wind-down

aspirations: Win matches comfortably against friends, colleagues, and family
Experience chess as an intellectual stress-reliever rather than an exercise in frustration
frustrations: Furious when losing a 25-move advantage due to a single stupid blunder
Disheartened after watching hours of educational YouTube videos only to drop 50 rating points in the evening
Intimidated by dense notation books, Grandmaster lingo, and 20-move opening trees
Lack of structured time to sit through master classes
learningStyle: Hands-on trial and error: prefers touching and doing rather than listening to lectures
Instant gratification: needs immediate feedback loops on whether a move was sound
Gamified progress: motivated by streaks, completion bars, and clear milestones

behavioralArchetypes.name: The 'YouTube Binge' Plateau
behavioralArchetypes.traits: Watches hours of GothamChess, Daniel Naroditsky, or Hikaru recaps. Feels like they understand master-level chess, but in real games they immediately panic and hang a piece.

behavioralArchetypes.name: The 'Opening Trap' Victim
behavioralArchetypes.traits: Bought an opening course or memorized 10 moves of Queen's Gambit, only to be crushed by random beginner attacks and early Queen raids like Scholar's Mate variations.

behavioralArchetypes.name: The 'Busy Professional'
behavioralArchetypes.traits: Wants to get better in 15 minutes a day during coffee breaks; has zero interest in becoming a titled player, just wants to stop feeling embarrassed on Chess.com.

primaryPainPoint.coreProblem: The gap between knowing basic piece rules and surviving tactical blunders.
primaryPainPoint.analysis: Beginners learn how the pieces move in 10 minutes. But in live games, they lose not because they don't know the rules, and not because they don't know the Catalan opening, but because their brain has not developed the subconscious survival radar to spot undefended pieces, simple forks, and back-rank threats before clicking. Traditional courses throw opening theory and abstract pawn structure lectures at them, which is completely useless when 92% of games under 800 Elo are decided by an outright 1-move tactical blunder and hanging piece.
consequences: Rapid tilt and rating drops: losing winning positions creates emotional burnout.
Plateauing for 6–18 months at 500 Elo despite playing hundreds of games.
Wasted money on high-end video repertoires they abandon after chapter 1.

positioningStatement: For adult casual chess players stuck between 400 and 800 Elo who are exhausted from losing winning games to stupid tactical blunders, BlunderProof Chess is a zero-video, browser-first interactive survival course that builds instinctive danger radar in 15 minutes a day. Unlike passive master lectures and opening theory drills, our active bite-sized simulator trains your brain to protect pieces, spot killer forks, and punish opponent mistakes through pure hands-on board action.

uniqueValueProposition.headline: Stop hanging pieces. Start winning games. 100% action, zero video fluff.
uniqueValueProposition.subtext: The first interactive chess survival course engineered specifically to break the 400–800 rating plateau through active tactile muscle memory—no opening memorization required.
keyMetricsTargeted: Cut unforced piece blunders by 75% in 14 days
Achieve 1000 Elo milestone with just 15 minutes of daily interactive board reps
Zero hours wasted watching passive videos
